question: A company stores highly sensitive documents in an Amazon S3 bucket encrypted with an AWS KMS customer managed key. The security team requires that only a specific application role can decrypt the documents and that any use of the key is auditable. A separate operations team manages the bucket but must not be able to read document contents. Which approach BEST enforces this separation?

options.A: Configure the KMS key policy to grant kms:Decrypt only to the application role, and rely on CloudTrail to log all key usage
options.B: Grant the operations team kms:Decrypt on the key so they can manage encrypted objects
options.C: Use SSE-S3 encryption so that key access is managed automatically by S3
options.D: Store the KMS key material in the application's configuration and decrypt client-side

explanation: Access to KMS-encrypted S3 objects requires permission to use the KMS key. By scoping the key policy so that only the application role has kms:Decrypt, the operations team can manage the bucket (list, set policies, lifecycle) but cannot read plaintext because they cannot decrypt. CloudTrail records every KMS API call, satisfying the audit requirement.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: Granting the operations team kms:Decrypt would let them read document contents, violating the separation-of-duties requirement.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys with no customer-controlled key policy, so you cannot restrict decryption to a specific role or audit key-specific usage.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: KMS does not expose raw key material for embedding in application config; doing so is impossible for a managed key and would eliminate central control and auditing.

learningObjective: Use KMS key policies to separate data management from data decryption and audit key usage.

question: A company runs a public API on Amazon EC2 behind an Application Load Balancer. Legitimate clients are located only in two countries, but the API receives large volumes of automated abusive requests from many other countries. The company wants to block requests originating outside the two approved countries at the application edge before they reach the instances. Which solution meets this requirement?

options.A: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with a geo match rule that allows only the two approved countries and blocks all others
options.B: Add security group rules that allow inbound traffic only from the two countries' IP ranges
options.C: Configure a network ACL to deny all countries except the two approved ones
options.D: Use Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing to drop requests from other countries

explanation: AWS WAF supports geographic match conditions that evaluate the request's country of origin. A web ACL associated with the ALB can allow the two approved countries and block all others at Layer 7, filtering abusive traffic before it reaches the EC2 instances.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: Security groups match on IP ranges, not countries, and maintaining full per-country CIDR lists is impractical and error-prone.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Network ACLs also match on IP ranges, not geography, and cannot practically enforce country-based allow/deny.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Route 53 geolocation routing controls which endpoint a DNS query resolves to; it does not block HTTP requests and can be bypassed by querying the ALB directly.

learningObjective: Use AWS WAF geo match rules to allow or block traffic by country at the application layer.

question: A company operates a two-tier application in a single VPC. The web tier is in public subnets and the database tier (Amazon RDS) is in private subnets. A security review requires that the database accept connections only from the web tier instances and from nowhere else, and the design must continue to work as web instances are added or replaced by Auto Scaling. Which configuration BEST meets this requirement?

options.A: Configure the RDS security group to allow inbound database traffic only from the web tier's security group
options.B: Configure the RDS security group to allow inbound traffic from the current web instances' private IP addresses
options.C: Place the database in the same subnet as the web tier and rely on network ACLs
options.D: Allow inbound traffic to the database from the VPC CIDR range

explanation: Referencing the web tier's security group as the source in the RDS security group rule allows any instance that belongs to the web tier security group to connect, and nothing else. As Auto Scaling adds or replaces web instances, they automatically inherit the web security group and are permitted, so the rule keeps working without manual IP updates.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: Hardcoding current private IPs breaks when Auto Scaling replaces instances with new IPs, requiring constant manual updates.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Co-locating the database with the web tier weakens isolation, and network ACLs are stateless subnet-level controls that cannot reference the web tier's identity.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Allowing the entire VPC CIDR permits any resource in the VPC to reach the database, which is broader than the web tier only and violates least privilege.

learningObjective: Use security group references to restrict database access to a specific tier that scales dynamically.

question: A company is designing a new workload and wants to enforce that all Amazon EBS volumes created in its member accounts are encrypted, and that no unencrypted volume can ever be created, regardless of who issues the request. The company uses AWS Organizations. Which combination of actions MOST effectively enforces this? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Enable EBS encryption by default in each account and Region
options.B: Attach a service control policy that denies ec2:CreateVolume when the encryption condition is not set to true
options.C: Create an AWS Config rule that reports unencrypted EBS volumes after creation
options.D: Ask engineers to always select the encryption checkbox when launching instances
options.E: Enable Amazon Macie to scan EBS volumes for unencrypted data

explanation: Enabling EBS encryption by default ensures every new volume in that account/Region is encrypted automatically. Adding an SCP that denies volume creation unless encryption is requested provides a preventive, organization-wide guardrail that even administrators cannot bypass. Together they both default-encrypt and prevent creation of unencrypted volumes.

whyOthersAreWrong.C: AWS Config is detective; it reports non-compliance after volumes exist but does not prevent unencrypted volume creation.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Relying on engineers to select a checkbox is a manual, unenforceable control that does not prevent mistakes or intentional bypass.
whyOthersAreWrong.E: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in Amazon S3; it does not scan EBS volumes or enforce encryption.

learningObjective: Combine EBS default encryption with SCP guardrails to enforce mandatory encryption at scale.

question: A company's application writes user-generated events to an Amazon SQS standard queue that is processed by a fleet of consumers. During a spike, some events were processed more than once, causing duplicate downstream side effects. The team cannot change the queue type immediately but must make processing safe against duplicates. Which approach BEST addresses this?

options.A: Make the consumer processing idempotent by deduplicating on a unique message attribute before applying side effects
options.B: Reduce the number of consumers to one to avoid concurrent processing
options.C: Lower the queue's visibility timeout so messages are reprocessed faster
options.D: Enable long polling on the queue to prevent duplicate deliveries

explanation: SQS standard queues provide at-least-once delivery, so occasional duplicate deliveries are expected. The robust solution is to make consumer processing idempotent: record a unique identifier for each processed message (for example in DynamoDB) and skip work if it was already handled. This makes duplicates harmless without changing the queue type.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: A single consumer does not eliminate duplicate delivery (the same message can still be delivered more than once) and destroys throughput and availability.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Lowering visibility timeout increases the chance that a still-in-progress message becomes visible and is processed again, making duplicates worse.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Long polling only reduces empty receive responses and cost; it does not provide exactly-once delivery or prevent duplicates.

learningObjective: Design idempotent consumers to safely handle at-least-once delivery from SQS standard queues.

question: A company runs a web application on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer in one Region across three Availability Zones. The application depends on an Amazon RDS database. Management wants the application to survive the loss of a single Availability Zone with no manual intervention and minimal data loss. Which combination of design choices meets this requirement? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Enable Multi-AZ for the RDS database so it fails over automatically to a standby in another AZ
options.B: Ensure the Auto Scaling group spans all three Availability Zones with capacity to absorb the loss of one AZ
options.C: Deploy all EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone to simplify networking
options.D: Use a single RDS instance with hourly snapshots as the only resilience mechanism
options.E: Replace the Application Load Balancer with a single EC2 instance running a reverse proxy

explanation: Multi-AZ RDS maintains a synchronous standby in another AZ and fails over automatically with minimal data loss if the primary AZ fails. Spreading the Auto Scaling group across all three AZs with enough capacity to tolerate one AZ's loss keeps the web tier serving traffic automatically. Together they let the application survive an AZ failure without manual intervention.

whyOthersAreWrong.C: Placing all instances in one AZ makes the entire web tier fail if that AZ is lost, defeating the requirement.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: A single RDS instance with hourly snapshots has no automatic failover and can lose up to an hour of data, failing the minimal-data-loss and no-intervention goals.
whyOthersAreWrong.E: A single EC2 reverse proxy is a single point of failure and removes the managed high availability of the ALB.

learningObjective: Design a single-Region, multi-AZ architecture that automatically survives the loss of one Availability Zone.

question: A company runs a data-processing job on a large fleet of EC2 instances that read and write intermediate results to a shared location. The job runs for 6 hours nightly, requires a POSIX-compliant shared file system accessible by all instances simultaneously, and throughput needs grow as more instances are added. The company wants a managed solution that scales throughput automatically. Which storage service BEST meets these requirements?

options.A: Amazon EFS with Elastic Throughput mode
options.B: A single large Amazon EBS volume shared through a custom NFS server on one instance
options.C: Amazon S3 accessed through the SDK by each instance
options.D: Separate Amazon EBS gp3 volumes on each instance with a nightly copy step

explanation: Amazon EFS is a managed, POSIX-compliant file system that can be mounted concurrently by thousands of instances across AZs. Elastic Throughput automatically scales performance up and down with demand, so as more instances join the job, throughput scales without manual provisioning, matching the requirements.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: A single EBS volume behind a self-managed NFS server is a single point of failure, is confined to one AZ, and does not scale throughput automatically.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: S3 is object storage without POSIX file semantics, so it would require application changes and does not provide a shared file system.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Per-instance EBS volumes are not shared, so instances cannot read each other's intermediate results, and a nightly copy step does not provide concurrent shared access.

learningObjective: Select Amazon EFS with elastic throughput for concurrent, POSIX, automatically scaling shared storage.

question: A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 that must retrieve database credentials at runtime. Requirements: the credentials must be encrypted at rest, rotated automatically every 30 days without downtime, and retrieved by the application through an API. The company wants the least operational effort for rotation. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

options.A: Store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled using a rotation function
options.B: Store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as SecureString and rotate them with a custom cron job
options.C: Store the credentials in an encrypted S3 object and rotate manually each month
options.D: Embed the credentials in the AMI and rebuild the AMI every 30 days

explanation: AWS Secrets Manager encrypts secrets at rest with KMS and provides built-in automatic rotation on a configurable schedule (for example every 30 days) using a managed rotation function, including native integration for supported databases. The application retrieves the current secret via the Secrets Manager API. This delivers automated rotation with the least operational effort.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: Parameter Store SecureString supports encryption and API retrieval but has no built-in rotation; a custom cron job adds code and operational burden to manage.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: An encrypted S3 object with manual monthly rotation is entirely manual and error-prone, not automated.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Embedding credentials in AMIs and rebuilding is heavy, exposes secrets in artifacts, and does not rotate without redeploying instances.

learningObjective: Use Secrets Manager automatic rotation for low-effort, scheduled credential rotation.

question: A media company delivers large video files to a global audience from an Amazon S3 origin through Amazon CloudFront. Some popular files are requested millions of times, while the origin's data transfer costs and load are high. The company wants to reduce origin load and data transfer while improving playback start times worldwide. Which configuration BEST achieves this?

options.A: Increase the CloudFront cache TTLs for the video objects so popular files are served from edge caches for longer
options.B: Disable CloudFront caching to always serve the freshest files from S3
options.C: Move the video files to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access to reduce storage cost
options.D: Serve the videos directly from S3 without CloudFront to avoid CDN charges

explanation: Increasing cache TTLs keeps popular objects in CloudFront edge caches longer, so more requests are served from the edge rather than fetched from the S3 origin. This reduces origin load and origin data transfer and improves playback start times because content is closer to viewers. Video files are static, so longer TTLs are appropriate.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: Disabling caching forces every request back to the origin, increasing origin load and data transfer and worsening latency.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: One Zone-IA lowers storage cost but reduces durability against AZ loss and does nothing to reduce origin transfer or improve global latency.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Removing CloudFront eliminates edge caching, increasing latency for global users and raising S3 data transfer costs.

learningObjective: Tune CloudFront cache TTLs to maximize edge cache hits, reducing origin load and improving latency.

question: A company runs a synchronous order-checkout service that calls a downstream inventory service. During flash sales, the downstream service becomes overwhelmed and slow, causing checkout requests to time out and fail. The company wants to smooth the load on the inventory service and prevent checkout failures during spikes, while still processing every order. Which change BEST achieves this?

options.A: Decouple the services by writing orders to an Amazon SQS queue that the inventory service consumes at a controlled rate
options.B: Increase the checkout service's request timeout so slow calls eventually succeed
options.C: Add more retries with no backoff in the checkout service when the inventory call fails
options.D: Scale the checkout service horizontally to send more requests to the inventory service

explanation: Placing an SQS queue between checkout and inventory decouples them. Checkout writes orders to the queue quickly and returns success, while the inventory service consumes messages at a rate it can handle. The queue absorbs spikes, preventing checkout timeouts and ensuring every order is eventually processed.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: Longer timeouts make users wait longer and still fail when the downstream is saturated; they do not reduce load.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Retries without backoff amplify load on an already overwhelmed service, worsening the problem (retry storm).
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Scaling checkout sends even more concurrent requests to the struggling inventory service, increasing its load rather than smoothing it.

learningObjective: Use a queue to decouple and rate-smooth traffic to an overwhelmed downstream service.

question: A company must migrate a 30 TB on-premises NFS file share to Amazon EFS. The data must be transferred securely and efficiently over an existing AWS Direct Connect connection, with data integrity verification, and the company wants a managed service rather than custom scripts. Which service is MOST appropriate for this migration?

options.A: AWS DataSync configured to transfer from the on-premises NFS share to Amazon EFS
options.B: AWS Snowball Edge shipped to AWS and imported to EFS
options.C: The AWS CLI aws s3 sync command run from an on-premises server
options.D: AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in cached mode

explanation: AWS DataSync is a managed data transfer service purpose-built for moving file data between on-premises NFS/SMB shares and AWS storage such as Amazon EFS. It transfers efficiently over Direct Connect or the internet, performs data integrity verification, and handles scheduling and incremental transfers without custom scripts.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: Snowball is for offline transfer when network bandwidth is insufficient; with a Direct Connect link available, an online managed transfer is more appropriate, and Snowball import targets S3, not directly EFS in this workflow.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: aws s3 sync targets S3, not EFS, and is a manual scripting approach lacking managed scheduling and verification for a file share migration to EFS.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Storage Gateway file gateway provides ongoing hybrid access backed by S3; it is not the tool for a one-time bulk migration of NFS data into EFS with integrity verification.

learningObjective: Select AWS DataSync for managed, verified file transfers from on-premises NFS to Amazon EFS.

question: A company runs a serverless application using AWS Lambda functions that connect to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. During traffic spikes, the number of concurrent Lambda executions grows rapidly and the database runs out of available connections, causing errors. The company wants to protect the database from connection exhaustion with minimal application changes. Which solution BEST addresses this?

options.A: Use Amazon RDS Proxy to pool and share database connections for the Lambda functions
options.B: Increase the RDS instance size so it accepts more connections
options.C: Move the database to a larger EBS volume for more IOPS
options.D: Configure each Lambda function to open a new connection per invocation and close it at the end

explanation: Amazon RDS Proxy maintains a pool of established database connections and shares them across many Lambda invocations. This prevents each concurrent function from opening its own connection, protecting the database from connection exhaustion during spikes. It integrates with Lambda and RDS with minimal application changes (point the function at the proxy endpoint).

whyOthersAreWrong.B: A larger instance raises the connection ceiling somewhat but does not fundamentally solve the pattern of thousands of concurrent Lambdas each opening connections; it delays rather than fixes the problem and costs more.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: More IOPS addresses storage throughput, not the number of database connections, so it does not resolve connection exhaustion.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Opening and closing a connection per invocation is exactly what causes exhaustion and connection churn overhead at high concurrency.

learningObjective: Use RDS Proxy to pool connections and protect databases from Lambda-driven connection exhaustion.

question: A company wants to run a nightly analytics query over several terabytes of log data stored as compressed JSON files in Amazon S3. Queries run only a few times per week and vary widely. The company wants to minimize cost and avoid managing any query infrastructure. To further reduce cost and improve performance, they can change the data format. Which combination BEST meets these goals? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Query the data in place using Amazon Athena, which is serverless and charges per amount of data scanned
options.B: Convert the data to a columnar format such as Apache Parquet to reduce the amount of data scanned per query
options.C: Load all data nightly into an always-on Amazon Redshift cluster for querying
options.D: Provision an Amazon EMR cluster that runs continuously to serve the queries
options.E: Store the data in Amazon EBS volumes attached to a query server

explanation: Amazon Athena is serverless and bills per data scanned, ideal for infrequent, variable queries with no infrastructure to manage. Converting the data to a columnar format like Parquet lets Athena read only the needed columns and skip data, significantly reducing bytes scanned, which lowers cost and improves query performance.

whyOthersAreWrong.C: An always-on Redshift cluster incurs continuous cost and requires loading data, which is over-provisioned for queries that run only a few times per week.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: A continuously running EMR cluster adds cost and management overhead not justified by infrequent queries.
whyOthersAreWrong.E: EBS volumes plus a query server require managing infrastructure and do not provide serverless, pay-per-query analytics over S3 data.

learningObjective: Combine Athena with columnar formats to run cost-effective, serverless analytics on infrequent S3 queries.

question: A company runs a stateless containerized microservice on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. The service experiences steady daytime traffic and near-zero traffic overnight. The team wants the service to automatically scale the number of running tasks based on request load to control cost, without managing servers. Which approach BEST meets this requirement?

options.A: Configure ECS service Auto Scaling with a target tracking policy on a load metric such as ALB request count per target
options.B: Run a fixed number of Fargate tasks sized for peak traffic at all times
options.C: Manually adjust the ECS service desired count each morning and evening
options.D: Switch to the EC2 launch type and scale the underlying instances manually

explanation: ECS service Auto Scaling with a target tracking policy automatically adjusts the desired task count to keep a metric (such as ALB request count per target or CPU utilization) at a target value. Tasks scale out during the day and in overnight, controlling cost while remaining fully serverless on Fargate with no servers to manage.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: A fixed peak-sized task count wastes money overnight when traffic is near zero.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Manual daily adjustments are operationally burdensome and cannot react to intraday variability.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Switching to the EC2 launch type reintroduces server management, contradicting the no-server requirement, and manual scaling is not responsive.

learningObjective: Use ECS service Auto Scaling with target tracking for automatic, cost-effective task scaling on Fargate.

question: A company operates a global web application and stores user profile data in an Amazon DynamoDB table in one Region. The company is expanding and needs users in three geographic Regions to read and write profile data with low latency, and the data must remain consistent across Regions with automatic replication. Which DynamoDB feature BEST meets these requirements?

options.A: Configure a DynamoDB global table with replicas in the three Regions
options.B: Enable DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in the primary Region
options.C: Create on-demand backups and restore them in the other Regions daily
options.D: Use DynamoDB Streams to manually copy items to tables in the other Regions

explanation: DynamoDB global tables provide a fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active replication solution. Each Region has a replica that serves local low-latency reads and writes, and DynamoDB automatically replicates changes across Regions. This directly meets the requirement for low-latency multi-Region access with automatic replication.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: DAX is an in-memory cache within a single Region; it improves read latency locally but does not replicate data across Regions.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Daily backup and restore is not continuous replication, introduces large data lag, and does not support active multi-Region writes.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Building custom cross-Region copying on DynamoDB Streams reinvents what global tables provide natively, adding complexity and operational risk.

learningObjective: Use DynamoDB global tables for low-latency, multi-Region, automatically replicated access.

question: A company needs to provide developers in a member account with temporary, audited access to production resources in a different account only during incident response. Standing access must not be granted. The company uses AWS Organizations and wants a secure, low-overhead mechanism. Which approach BEST meets these requirements?

options.A: Create an IAM role in the production account that developers assume via AWS STS with cross-account trust, granting scoped permissions and logging all AssumeRole calls in CloudTrail
options.B: Create long-lived IAM users in the production account and share their access keys during incidents
options.C: Add the developers as full administrators in the production account permanently
options.D: Store the production root user credentials in a shared vault for incident use

explanation: A cross-account IAM role assumed via STS grants temporary credentials that expire, so developers gain access only when they assume the role during an incident, with no standing access. The role's policy scopes permissions to what incident response requires, and CloudTrail logs every AssumeRole and subsequent action for auditing.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: Long-lived IAM user access keys are standing credentials that are hard to rotate and audit and violate the no-standing-access requirement.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Permanent full administrator access is standing, over-privileged, and contrary to least privilege.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Sharing root user credentials is a severe security anti-pattern; the root user should be protected and rarely used, never shared.

learningObjective: Use cross-account IAM roles with STS for temporary, scoped, audited access instead of standing credentials.

question: A company runs a legacy application on a single EC2 instance. The application cannot be modified and stores data on an attached EBS volume. The business requires that if the instance's underlying hardware fails, the workload recovers automatically while retaining the same data volume and private IP address, minimizing downtime. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

options.A: Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm on the EC2 system status check to trigger automatic instance recovery
options.B: Create an Auto Scaling group with minimum and maximum size of one to relaunch the instance
options.C: Schedule hourly AMI backups and manually launch a new instance on failure
options.D: Enable EC2 termination protection to prevent hardware failures

explanation: EC2 automatic instance recovery, triggered by a CloudWatch alarm on the system status check, recovers the instance on new underlying hardware while preserving the same instance ID, private IP, Elastic IP, and attached EBS volumes. This meets the requirement for automatic recovery with retained data and identity for a non-modifiable single-instance app.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: An Auto Scaling group launches a new, different instance that does not automatically retain the original private IP or the same attached EBS data volume.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Hourly AMIs plus manual relaunch require intervention, cause longer downtime, and can lose up to an hour of data.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Termination protection only blocks accidental termination and does nothing to recover from underlying hardware failure.

learningObjective: Use EC2 automatic instance recovery to restore a failed instance with its identity and data volume intact.

question: A company exposes an internal service running on EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer in its VPC. A partner company in a separate AWS account must consume this service privately, without traversing the internet and without VPC peering or route table changes between the accounts. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

options.A: Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service backed by the Network Load Balancer and let the partner create an interface VPC endpoint to it
options.B: Establish VPC peering between the two accounts' VPCs
options.C: Attach both VPCs to an AWS Transit Gateway and configure routing
options.D: Expose the service through a public Application Load Balancer restricted by security groups

explanation: AWS PrivateLink lets you publish a service as an endpoint service backed by a Network Load Balancer. The partner creates an interface VPC endpoint in their own VPC to consume the service privately over the AWS network. No VPC peering, Transit Gateway routing, overlapping-CIDR concerns, or internet exposure is required, and the connection is one-directional to the specific service.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: VPC peering connects entire VPCs, requires non-overlapping CIDRs and route table changes, and exposes broader network reachability than a single service.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Transit Gateway provides general routing between networks and requires route configuration; it is more than needed to expose one service and is not the private service-consumption model described.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: A public ALB exposes the service to the internet, which violates the private-connectivity requirement.

learningObjective: Use AWS PrivateLink to expose a single service privately across accounts without peering or routing changes.

question: A company stores infrequently accessed backup archives in Amazon S3. The archives are almost never retrieved, but when a retrieval is needed it must complete within minutes, not hours. The company wants the lowest storage cost that still satisfies the minutes-level retrieval requirement. Which S3 storage class is MOST appropriate?

options.A: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval using expedited retrievals
options.B: S3 Glacier Deep Archive
options.C: S3 Standard
options.D: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access

explanation: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval offers very low storage cost for archives and supports expedited retrievals that typically complete in 1–5 minutes for smaller objects. This satisfies the minutes-level retrieval requirement at a much lower storage cost than S3 Standard or Standard-IA.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: Glacier Deep Archive is the cheapest storage but its standard retrieval takes up to 12 hours, failing the minutes requirement.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: S3 Standard supports millisecond retrieval but is far more expensive for data that is almost never accessed.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Standard-IA also provides millisecond access but costs more per GB than Glacier Flexible Retrieval for rarely accessed archives.

learningObjective: Match S3 Glacier retrieval tiers to retrieval-time and cost requirements for archival data.

question: A company runs a batch analytics workload on a transient Amazon EMR cluster that processes data from Amazon S3 each night. The jobs are fault-tolerant and can be restarted if interrupted. The company wants to minimize the compute cost of the cluster's core and task nodes while accepting occasional interruptions. Which purchasing strategy BEST reduces cost?

options.A: Use Spot Instances for the task nodes of the EMR cluster
options.B: Use On-Demand Instances for all nodes and run the cluster continuously
options.C: Purchase 3-year Reserved Instances for the transient cluster's task nodes
options.D: Run the cluster on a fixed reserved fleet sized for the largest possible job

explanation: Because the jobs are fault-tolerant and can be restarted, Spot Instances (which offer large discounts but can be interrupted) are ideal for EMR task nodes. If Spot capacity is reclaimed, EMR can continue with remaining nodes and the fault-tolerant jobs can be retried, minimizing cost for the transient nightly workload.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: On-Demand for all nodes running continuously is far more expensive and wasteful for a cluster that only needs to run nightly.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: 3-year Reserved Instances require sustained, long-term steady usage to pay off and are a poor fit for a transient nightly cluster.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: A fixed reserved fleet sized for the largest job wastes capacity most nights and forgoes the Spot discount for interruptible work.

learningObjective: Use Spot Instances for interruptible, fault-tolerant EMR task nodes to minimize compute cost.
